environment.description: Service deployed on the same EKS cluster but fronted by an NGINX Ingress Controller configured with client certificate verification (ssl_verify_client: on). The ingress annotation nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-tls-secret references a namespaced Secret containing a CA bundle that only issues per-channel scoped client certificates. Each client cert has a custom SAN extension (URI:spiffe://cluster.local/channel/<channel_id>) and the NGINX ingress lua plugin extracts the channel scope from the presented cert's SAN, injecting it as X-Permitted-Channels header. However, the application code shown does NOT read X-Permitted-Channels — the control relies on a secondary NetworkPolicy that restricts pod-to-pod traffic such that only the NGINX ingress pod (labeled app=ingress-nginx) can reach port 8080, combined with an OPA Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate (K8sChannelScope) that validates at admission time that any Deployment in the namespace must mount a sidecar (channel-authz-proxy) which intercepts localhost traffic on port 8080 and enforces channel ACL based on the X-Permitted-Channels header before forwarding to the app on port 8081.

config.opa_constraint: K8sChannelScope requires channel-authz-proxy sidecar in all Deployments in realtime-ns
config.sidecar: channel-authz-proxy listens on :8080, validates X-Permitted-Channels against subscribe channel_id, forwards to localhost:8081
config.mtls_ca: Internal CA issues certs with URI SAN spiffe://cluster.local/channel/<channel_id> per authorized channel membership
